summary: The comment argues for a federal requirement to allow parents meaningful opt-out of screen-based instruction in schools, citing evidence from the author's own experience and research showing the benefits of parental choice in this context. The text discusses concerns about the use of digital devices and AI in education, highlighting negative impacts on learning and privacy. It cites research showing that screen time can reduce reading comprehension, retention, and exam performance. Parents are raising concerns about data collection and lack of transparency. The text argues against imposing screen-time limits or restrictions on E-Rate funding, emphasizing the need for parental autonomy and the precautionary principle. The comment argues against requiring an opt-out from screen-based instruction for parents, emphasizing the importance of parental autonomy and the need for a guaranteed opt-out option.
